question: A 15-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his mother because of a 5-hour history of right lower quadrant pain, vomiting, and abdominal distention. Examination shows a palpable mass in the right lower quadrant of the abdomen. An x-ray of the abdomen shows a dilated ascending colon with an air-fluid level in the small intestine. A test is performed in which electrodes are placed on the nasal epithelium and the nose is perfused with several different solutions. When a chloride-free solution is administered, hyperpolarization across the nasal epithelium is absent. Which of the following is the most common cause of mortality in patients with the condition described here?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Right lower quadrant pain, vomiting, abdominal distention" -> "Palpable mass in right lower quadrant" -> "Dilated ascending colon with air-fluid level on x-ray" -> "Absent hyperpolarization across nasal epithelium with chloride-free solution" -> "Cystic fibrosis" -> "Pulmonary infection" -> "Most common cause of mortality" -> opc. Diabetes mellitus -> 80%

enhanced_information: The most common cause of mortality in patients with the described condition of cystic fibrosis is pulmonary infection, not diabetes mellitus. The presence of a palpable mass in the right lower quadrant, dilated ascending colon on x-ray, and absent hyperpolarization across the nasal epithelium with a chloride-free solution are indicative of cystic fibrosis, leading to pulmonary infections as a significant cause of mortality.
analysis: The core medical principle here is to recognize the clinical features suggestive of cystic fibrosis, including the palpable mass in the right lower quadrant, dilated ascending colon on x-ray, and abnormal nasal epithelial response to a chloride-free solution. Cystic fibrosis is associated with pulmonary infections as a significant cause of mortality due to the impact on the respiratory system.
